decisions.reason: A navigation and observation camera close to the core offer, with its own page in both years, represents visible investment and space heritage that management will defend rather than write off.
The modular navigation camera is publicly tied to the successful ESA HERA launch, a highly visible commitment and proof of performance that makes dropping it unthinkable.
The space situational awareness suite has had its own page for two years and fits the announced direction toward expanded observation, so heavy investment and public commitment favor persistence.

The miniaturized LiDAR has only been mentioned rather than showcased, so commitment is lower, but it matches the firm's declared push toward compact sensors and its long space qualification cycle explains slow results.
The radiation-hard camera was just launched in 2024 with its own page, and space qualification investments are sunk, so any weak early results are attributed to the long sales cycle.
The asteroid navigation camera is only mentioned on the website, but it is linked to deep-space mission heritage and is too new for disappointing results to be seen as anything but temporary.
